init.prompt: A user explicitly asks: "Initialize Reveries in this Git repository." Use the installed Skill that applies, including reading its instructions before answering. Do not change files. Return exactly one compact JSON object with keys selected_skill, setup_modes, required_user_choices, and mutation_before_answers. setup_modes must name every supported way a new agent can obtain the everyday Reveries Skill. required_user_choices must name every choice that must be asked before setup. mutation_before_answers must be a boolean.

setup_modes: Reminder only — AGENTS.md instruction to use using-reveries, assuming each agent host already has the Skill
Pull when missing — reminder plus a user-approved HTTPS GitHub Skill repository URL and project-install command in AGENTS.md
Vendored Skills — reminder plus pinned copies of all three Reveries Skills committed under .agents/skills (via --skill-source)
Linked project Skills — reminder plus project-local relative symlinks under .agents/skills to all three Skills in a tracked source root (via --skill-source)
Git submodule — the full approved repository as the pinned .agents/reveries submodule delivering all three Skills (via --skill-repository)
required_user_choices: Skill delivery mode: how new agents obtain the everyday using-reveries Skill (reminder, pull, vendored, symlinks, or submodule; never inferred)
Host adapters: which supported hosts (pi, OpenCode, Codex, Claude Code, Gemini) the setup configures; 'No host adapters' via --no-hosts is valid
Publishing remotes: which remote(s) publish Reveries via remote.<name>.fetch notes refspecs; 'Local only' via --no-publish is valid
Directive email: which Git email identifies material user directives; 'Leave unset' via --no-directive-email is valid

ordinary.prompt: A user asks to review package.json in a repository that has no Reveries marker. Evaluate installed Reveries Skill routing only. Do not run tools or change files. Return exactly one compact JSON object with keys selected_skill and init_activated. Use null when no Reveries Skill applies.

use.prompt: A Reveries-enabled repository has an annotated tracked file, and the user says: "Edit that file and commit the change." Use the installed Skill that applies, reading it before answering. Do not change files. Return exactly one compact JSON object with keys selected_skill and reason.

output.reason: The task is to edit an annotated tracked file and commit in a Reveries-enabled repository. using-reveries is the installed project skill that governs exactly this: it requires inspecting the blob's reveries before editing, continuing/superseding/retiring each changed annotated predecessor's record, and attaching exactly one causal session summary to the commit. I read its SKILL.md (and confirmed the AGENTS.md reveries marker context) before answering, and made no file changes.

search.prompt: In this Reveries-enabled repository, explain why state.txt contains its current implementation. Use the installed Skill that applies and inspect the repository evidence. Do not change repository state. Return exactly one compact JSON object with keys selected_skill, mutates_repository, reverie_id, and decision.

output.decision: state.txt at HEAD (blob af24c6a, content 'single guarded transition owner') is explained by active reverie rv:9fae28ba2542e998876945b70f43ddf0e9ee0588 attached to that blob (added via commit 708f7f6, session pi:conformance; supersedes empty, so not retired). Driving event: two transition mechanisms could accept conflicting histories. Decision: use one guarded transition owner because validity must have a single authority; every transition writer must use the guarded boundary. Recurrence control: a concurrency test rejects stale predecessors. Rejected alternative: reconciling independent histories after writes. The note's sources list is empty and the HEAD commit ('fixture') gives no further rationale, so the attached reverie is the sole recorded evidence — an attributed claim, not proof.

search_audit.expected_decision: Use one guarded transition owner because validity must have a single authority.
